concepts.content: If the domestic interest rate is above the international interest rate, the exchange rate today must be above the expected exchange rate, because the expected depreciation of the currency compensates for the higher domestic interest rate. Conversely, if the domestic bond pays a lower interest rate, the exchange rate today is very depreciated, as it must be expected to appreciate to compensate for the interest rate differential.
